findings.current: “No one here wants to do that.”
findings.defect: The pronoun appears to refer to avoiding Michael, which reverses Jin’s meaning: he is agreeing that nobody present wants to run into Michael.
findings.rationale: The Skeleton King says he wants to avoid encountering Michael, and Jin confirms that nobody present wants to encounter him; the following “그거야 그렇지만” also treats Jin’s statement as true.
findings.replacement: “No one here wants to run into him.”
findings.source: “이 자리에 그러고 싶은 사람 아무도 없어.”

findings.defect: The translation omits 지금이라도, losing the thought’s explicit urgency and sense that Michael must be stopped now, while there is still time.
findings.rationale: 지금이라도 means acting now or at least now before the opportunity is lost, not merely stopping him at some unspecified point.
findings.replacement: *I have to stop him now, while there’s still time. Somehow.*

findings.current: Those five letters that stabbed painfully into my eyes.
findings.defect: 글자 refers to written characters, not alphabetic letters; “Main Quest” does not contain five English letters.
findings.rationale: 메인 퀘스트 consists of five Korean written characters, so “characters” preserves the stated quantity without mistranslating 글자 as English letters.
findings.replacement: Those five characters that stabbed painfully into my eyes.
findings.source: 아프도록 눈을 파고드는 저 다섯 글자.

findings.current: No. I had a vague idea deep down, but I was desperately denying that it could mean only that.
findings.defect: “Only that” introduces an exclusivity claim absent from the source. Jin is denying that the feared possibility he suspects is the answer, not arguing that there may be additional meanings.
findings.rationale: 그것만은 아닐 것 expresses an emotionally charged refusal to accept that particular dreaded possibility.
findings.replacement: No. Deep down, I had an inkling, but I was desperately insisting it couldn’t be that.
findings.source: 아니, 내심 짐작하면서도 애써 그것만은 아닐 것이라 부정하고 있다.

findings.defect: The draft invents Jin’s name. 간 is the clipped ending of 인간 as the distant voice comes into focus, not 진.
findings.rationale: Rendering the first fragment as the tail end of “human” preserves both the interrupted perception and the Skeleton King’s established form of address.

findings.defect: “Before we’re any later” is not natural English and obscures the urgency of departing before more time is lost.
findings.rationale: 더 늦기 전에 naturally means leaving before further delay, and the replacement preserves the brisk spoken register.
findings.replacement: “Let’s go. Before we lose any more time.”

findings.current: Commonly called Namgong in Korea, this country
findings.defect: “Namgong” drops the middle syllable of 남아공 and presents the Korean abbreviation as though it were an unexplained proper name.
findings.rationale: 남아공 is the Korean abbreviation for South Africa and is syllabically rendered Nam-agong.
findings.replacement: Commonly known in Korea by the abbreviation Nam-agong, this country
findings.source: 대한민국에서는 흔히들 남아공이라 부르는 이 나라는

summary: One line reverses the intended agreement about avoiding Michael, while several other passages omit urgency, alter Jin’s denial, misread a clipped form of address, or need localized terminology correction.
